The '''1708 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 10th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[United Delet]], across [[New Ayre]], from 2 June to 30 June 1708, and was the first edition of the competition to be staged outside [[Ayuma]] or [[Atirha]].<ref name="flla-overview">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/overview|title=1708 FLLA World Cup: tournament overview|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 March 1763}}</ref> Sixteen teams contested the finals, drawn from the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]], across 33 matches in eight host cities.

[[United Delet]] won the tournament, defeating [[Raledria]] 3–1 in the [[#Final|final]] at the Mantraal Federal Ground to claim their first World Cup title, and became the first nation affiliated to the [[NAFVL]] to be crowned champions.<ref name="flla-final-report">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/final-report|title=United Delet crowned 1708 FLLA World Cup champions|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 July 1708}}</ref> The result was an exact reversal of the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 final]], in which Raledria had beaten United Delet by the same 3–1 scoreline; for the hosts the victory was widely portrayed as the redemption of that earlier defeat. The two pre-tournament favourites, the defending champions [[Emara]] and the five-time finalists [[Lycroa]], were both eliminated at the semi-final stage, Emara by the hosts and Lycroa by Raledria, an outcome remembered in [[New Ayre|New Ayrean]] arraby literature as "the Ayren upset".

A total of 89 goals were scored across the 33 matches at an average of 2.70 per match. United Delet were the leading goalscoring side with 14 goals, and the home forward Joren Khaldari was later recognised as the tournament's top scorer with six. As 1708 fell between the destruction of the original [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] in the [[Red War]] and the introduction of the present rotating cup in [[1716 FLLA World Cup|1716]], the champions received a single bespoke permanent trophy, '''The Esrenva''', commissioned by the host federation and retained by United Delet in perpetuity.<ref name="flla-trophy">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/trophies/permanent-trophy-register|title=Register of FLLA World Cup permanent trophies|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 July 1764}}</ref>

The 1708 edition is also remembered as the first FLLA World Cup to be widely covered by photojournalists from across the seven confederations, with selected fixtures relayed by short-range radio to neighbouring nations.<ref name="factbook-1708">{{cite web|url=https://www.andahfactbook.org/sport/1708-world-cup|title=The 1708 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[The Andah Factbook]]|date=20 January 1764}}</ref>

==Host selection==

[[United Delet]] was confirmed as the host of the 1708 FLLA World Cup by a vote of the [[FLLA]] Council in the spring of 1705, in what was the first occasion on which the right to stage the competition had been awarded to a nation outside [[Ayuma]] or [[Atirha]]. The decision followed the FLLA Council's stated intention, adopted at the rebranding of the competition for the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 edition]], that future tournaments should be held outside Ayuma on a regular basis. The United Delet Arraby Federation's proposal was supported by the young [[NAFVL]], which had been admitted to the FLLA only in the preceding decade, and was the first major intercontinental fixture to be staged in [[New Ayre]].<ref name="flla-host">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/host-selection|title=United Delet awarded the 1708 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=6 April 1763}}</ref>

The award was not without misgivings within the Council. The principal concern was the distance between New Ayre and the established arraby nations of Ayuma and Atirha: visiting teams faced sea crossings of over two weeks, and several associations argued that the travel demands would depress the size and competitiveness of the field. In the event sixteen nations took part, the same number as at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700]] and [[1704 FLLA World Cup|1704 editions]], although the entry was drawn disproportionately from the two founding confederations, the [[AYFVL]] and the [[ATFVL]], which between them supplied nine of the sixteen finalists.<ref name="flla-host" />

In its bid the United Delet Arraby Federation pledged a programme of stadium construction and improvement across eight cities, with a combined budget of {{lahn}}60&nbsp;million drawn from the national treasury and the participating municipalities. As part of the same commission the Federation engaged the Mantraal sculptor Iresa Mondel to design the tournament's permanent trophy, The Esrenva, which under the arrangements then in force was to be the only senior award presented to the champions.<ref name="flla-esrenva">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/trophies/the-esrenva|title=The Esrenva: the permanent trophy of the 1708 FLLA World Cup|publisher=United Delet Arraby Federation|date=18 May 1763}}</ref>

==Participating teams and officials==

===Qualification===
[[File:1708 FLLA World Cup qualification.png|thumb|upright=1.5|{{legend|#000cff|Countries qualified for World Cup}} {{legend|#ffb400|Country did not qualify}} {{legend|black|Countries that did not enter the World Cup or were expelled from the tournament by FLLA prior to playing a match}} {{legend|#ababab|Country not a FLLA member}}]]

Sixteen places at the finals were allocated across the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]]. The allocation reflected both the size of each confederation and the practical difficulty of reaching [[New Ayre]]: the great majority of berths were given to the two founding confederations, with single places reserved for each of the four most recently admitted bodies and an enlarged share for the host confederation. The host nation, [[United Delet]], qualified automatically. Each confederation administered its own qualifying competition; full results are recorded on the individual confederation pages.

The qualified teams, by confederation, were:

===Seeding and draw===

The draw for the group stage was conducted in [[Mantraal]] in February 1708. In the absence of any established ranking system, the four seeded teams were determined on the basis of recent results: the hosts [[United Delet]], the defending champions [[Emara]], the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700]] champions [[Raledria]] and the most-decorated nation [[Lycroa]] were each placed at the head of one of the four groups, with the remaining twelve teams distributed on geographical lines so as to spread the confederations across the groups.<ref name="flla-draw">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/draw|title=The 1708 FLLA World Cup draw|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1763}}</ref>

===Officials===

The FLLA appointed a panel of twelve referees for the tournament, drawn from nine nations and including, for the first time, officials affiliated to confederations other than the [[AYFVL]] and [[ATFVL]]. Because matches were played without artificial lighting, all fixtures were scheduled for afternoon kick-offs and the panel worked to a compressed match programme across the eight venues. The opening match between [[United Delet]] and [[Iainoa]] was refereed by Tomas Eldis of [[Eldjo]]; the [[#Final|final]] was taken by Karel Vasmund of [[Praesyu]], whose national side had been eliminated in the quarter-finals.<ref name="flla-officials">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/officials|title=Match officials of the 1708 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1763}}</ref>

==Venues==

Eight stadiums in eight host cities were used in the final tournament, all located in [[United Delet]]. The largest was the Mantraal Federal Ground in the principal city of [[Mantraal]], which staged the opening match, one semi-final and the final, and which set a record for the largest attendance at any international arraby fixture when 41,800 spectators watched the final, surpassing the 38,000 recorded at the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 final]]. The remaining seven grounds, each staging group-stage matches and in four cases a knockout tie, ranged in capacity between roughly 19,000 and 29,000.<ref name="flla-venues">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/venues|title=Host stadiums of the 1708 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 May 1763}}</ref>

==Format==

The sixteen qualified teams were divided into four groups of four for the group stage. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; two points were awarded for a win and one for a draw, in line with the scoring system then in use across the competition. The top two teams from each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] and the bottom two were eliminated.

Under the regulations of the period, goal difference was not used to separate teams level on points for a qualifying place. Where two teams finished a group on equal points and the issue of qualification turned on the result, a single play-off match was staged at a neutral venue; this provision was invoked once during the tournament, in [[#Group 2|Group 2]]. Where a team's position was not in doubt, ties were left unresolved.

In the knockout stage, fixtures were single-elimination ties played over 90 minutes. Ties level at the end of normal time were extended by a 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; a tie still level after extra time would have been replayed, although no knockout match in 1708 required a replay. The two semi-final losers contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on the day before the final.

==Group stage==

The group stage was played between 2 and 14 June 1708. [[United Delet]] and [[Emara]] both won their groups with a perfect record, while [[Group 2]] required a play-off to separate [[Quidic]] and [[Etirha]], who finished level on points behind Emara. All four seeded teams advanced to the knockout stage.

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the eight teams that advanced from the group stage. The four group winners were drawn against the four group runners-up, with each tie pairing teams from different groups. Matches level after 90 minutes were extended by a period of extra time; one of the four quarter-finals, between [[Raledria]] and [[Praesyu]], required additional time, while the remaining seven ties were settled inside ninety minutes.

===Final===
{{Main|1708 FLLA World Cup final}}

The final was played on 30 June 1708 at the Mantraal Federal Ground before a record crowd of 41,800. [[United Delet]] took the lead through Joren Khaldari in the 26th minute and doubled their advantage through Davron Solani early in the second half; [[Raledria]] pulled a goal back through Anders Brask, before Esmir Vairos restored the two-goal margin in the closing stages to seal a 3–1 victory. The scoreline exactly reversed the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|1700 final]], in which Raledria had defeated United Delet 3–1, and made United Delet the first [[NAFVL]] nation to win the FLLA World Cup.<ref name="flla-final-report" />

==Goalscorers==

A total of 89 goals were scored across the 33 matches of the tournament, an average of 2.70 per match. The hosts [[United Delet]] were the leading goalscoring side with 14 goals; their forward Joren Khaldari finished as the tournament's top scorer with six. The principal scorers were:<ref name="flla-stats">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/1708/statistics|title=1708 FLLA World Cup statistics|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=14 March 1763}}</ref>

;6 goals
* {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Joren Khaldari ([[United Delet]])
;5 goals
* {{Flagicon|Raledria}} Anders Brask ([[Raledria]])
* {{Flagicon|Emara}} Aldric Venn ([[Emara]])
;4 goals
* {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Davron Solani ([[United Delet]])
* {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Esmir Vairos ([[United Delet]])
* {{Flagicon|Emara}} Caspar Holt ([[Emara]])
;3 goals
* {{Flagicon|Lycroa}} Mariano Velli ([[Lycroa]])
* {{Flagicon|Lycroa}} Tomaso Renn ([[Lycroa]])
* {{Flagicon|Raledria}} Niko Vossen ([[Raledria]])

A further nineteen players scored between one and two goals each.

==Awards==

The individual awards of the FLLA World Cup, the '''FLLA Vairan Ball''' for the best player, the '''FLLA Marskval''' for the leading goalscorer and the '''FLLA Bastion''' for the best goalkeeper, were not instituted in their modern form until [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744]]. The honorees listed below were conferred retrospectively by the FLLA when, following the formalisation of the awards, it reviewed the earlier editions of the competition and recognised the outstanding individual performances of each tournament.<ref name="flla-awards">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/heritage/world-cup/retrospective-awards|title=Retrospective individual awards of the early FLLA World Cups|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=9 August 1764}}</ref>

* '''FLLA Vairan Ball''' (best player): {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Kavi Mirovan ([[United Delet]]), the host side's midfielder and captain.
* '''FLLA Marskval''' (top scorer): {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Joren Khaldari ([[United Delet]]), six goals.
* '''FLLA Bastion''' (best goalkeeper): {{Flagicon|United Delet}} Lokan Tavalan ([[United Delet]]), who conceded four goals in six matches.

==Legacy==

The 1708 FLLA World Cup established that the competition could be staged successfully beyond the founding continents of [[Ayuma]] and [[Atirha]], and is generally credited with securing the long-term place of the [[NAFVL]] within the senior international game. United Delet's victory remained the only FLLA World Cup won by a [[New Ayre|New Ayrean]] nation until well into the modern era, and the country did not reach another final, although it hosted the tournament for a second time at the [[1752 FLLA World Cup|1752 edition]].<ref name="factbook-1708" /> The Esrenva, the permanent trophy of the edition, remains on public display at the United Delet Federal Gallery in [[Mantraal]].<ref name="flla-esrenva" />
